angle_name: Harmonic-tiling block variance: Saffari–Vaughan/Selberg short-interval variance imported block-wise onto the reciprocal-interval collapse identity
mechanism: Start from the already-kernel-formalized collapse identity (PrimeSieveAbelIdentity.lean): S := Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)R(⌊x/d⌋) = Σ_{e≤K} M(e)·Δ_e + M(K)R(y), where Δ_e = R(x/e) − R(x/(e+1)) is the prime-count discrepancy on the reciprocal interval I_e = (x/(e+1), x/e], of length H_e ≍ x/e². The structural observation of this lens: for e in a dyadic block [E,2E], the intervals I_e are DISJOINT, of comparable length H ≍ x/E², and they exactly tile the t-window [x/2E, x/E] of length X_w ≍ x/E — so Σ_{e∈[E,2E]} Δ_e² is a discrete short-interval prime variance over a tiling, precisely the object Selberg/Saffari–Vaughan/Montgomery–Soundararajan technology controls, except sampled on the harmonic mesh t = x/e rather than a uniform one. Compare the discrete tiling variance to the continuous integral of (ψ(t+H)−ψ(t)−H)² over the window by the standard overlapping-interval argument, sub-dividing each block into sub-blocks where H_e varies by 1+o(1). Unconditionally, via Huxley-type zero density, the continuous variance carries an exp(−c(log)^{c'}) saving whenever H ≥ X_w^{1/6+ε}; the condition x/E² ≥ (x/E)^{1/6+ε} holds for all E ≤ x^{5/11−ε}, i.e. most of the block range. Assemble in three zones: (i) low blocks e ≤ E₀ = exp((log x)^{1/2}): direct triangle inequality with the Vinogradov–Korobov PNT error on each long interval; (ii) middle blocks E₀ ≤ E ≤ x^{5/11−ε}: per-block Cauchy–Schwarz |Σ M(e)Δ_e| ≤ (Σ M(e)²)^{1/2}(Σ Δ_e²)^{1/2}, using the unconditional Landau/Walfisz bound M(e) ≪ e·exp(−c(log e)^{3/5−ε}) on the first factor and the tiling-variance bound Σ Δ_e² ≪ (x²/E³)·δ_V(x) on the second, giving per-block ≪ x·√(δ_M δ_V); (iii) tail blocks x^{5/11} < E ≤ K ≍ √x (intervals shorter than X_w^{1/6}: the pair-correlation regime, no unconditional variance known): bound by total variation, Σ_{e∈block}|Δ_e| ≤ π-mass + Li-mass ≪ (x/E)/log x, times max|M(e)| ≪ E·δ_M, giving ≪ x·δ_M/log x per block. Summing ≍ log x blocks yields an unconditional bound S ≪ x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}) with no lost log-factor — strictly o() of the honest trivial bound x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε})·log x obtained by termwise triangle inequality. Crucially, I ran the 𝔉-consistency check on my own recombination: feeding RH-strength inputs (M(e) ≪ e^{1/2+ε}, Selberg variance Σ Δ_e² ≪ X_w log²) into the block Cauchy–Schwarz gives per-block E^{1/2}x^{1/2}log, maximized at E = √x: exactly x^{3/4} — the F(1/2) = 3/4 wall. So this mechanism is honestly rung-0/near-rung-1 machinery; its second contribution is to isolate the exact 𝔉-exit coordinate: the signed block covariance C(E) = Σ_{e∈[E,2E]} M(e)Δ_e, a Möbius–prime short-interval correlation (equivalently Σ_{y<p≤x} M(⌊x/p⌋) minus its Li-average), which is the object Montgomery–Soundararajan first/mixed-moment (singular-series) technology would next address, conditionally.
new_leverage: Two things not already in the packet's frame. (1) The reciprocal intervals I_e, viewed block-dyadically, are a disjoint TILING with locally comparable lengths — this converts the pinned Abel sum into a family of genuine short-interval variance objects to which fifty years of Selberg/Saffari–Vaughan/Huxley/Montgomery–Soundararajan technology applies verbatim, with the internal e-average substituting for the external t-average those theorems need; no averaging over x is introduced. (2) The exponent map of the lens is computable in advance: the unconditional zero-density input (Huxley 12/5) fixes the exact crossover E = x^{5/11} between the variance-controlled zone and the pair-correlation tail, and the RH-input consistency check reproduces the 𝔉 wall x^{3/4} exactly, which both validates the audit and pins the residual difficulty onto one named signed object C(E). UNVERIFIED speculation throughout, per protocol.
target_estimate: Named estimate: BLOCK-TILED SAFFARI–VAUGHAN BOUND. Fix x, y ≍ √x, K = ⌊x/(y+1)⌋. Variables: dyadic block parameter E ∈ [1, K], window X_w = x/E, interval length H = x/E² (varying by factor ≤ 4 inside a block; sub-block so it varies by 1+o(1)). Claim A (variance): for exp((log x)^{1/2}) ≤ E ≤ x^{5/11−ε}, Σ_{E<e≤2E} (R(x/e) − R(x/(e+1)))² ≪ (x²/E³)·exp(−c(log x)^{1/3}) unconditionally, losses: comparison of discrete tiling variance to the continuous ψ-integral costs an absolute constant plus one (log x)^{O(1)} factor absorbed into the exponential saving; π-vs-ψ conversion costs O(√(x/E)·log) per interval, negligible in this range. Claim B (assembly): consequently, unconditionally, |Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)R(⌊x/d⌋)| ≪ x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}), with the three-zone split at E₀ = exp((log x)^{1/2}) and E₁ = x^{5/11−ε}; the binding loss is the Landau/Walfisz Mertens saving δ_M = exp(−c(log)^{3/5−ε}) in zones (i) and (iii), and √(δ_M δ_V) in zone (ii). Explicitly NOT claimed: any power-of-x exponent; the RH-input version of the same pipeline caps at x^{3/4}(log x), the 𝔉 wall.

obstacle_positions.F_closure: Inside 𝔉 for the exponent game, and I verified it: my only Mertens input is an L²/L∞ bound on M and my recombination is block Cauchy–Schwarz; with σ = 1/2 inputs the pipeline lands at exactly x^{3/4} = F(1/2), confirming the audit rather than evading it. I use the 𝔉-class machinery only where it is not vacuous: sub-power (PNT-strength) savings, which the closure theorem does not forbid. The μ×R sign interaction is deliberately forfeited in my deliverable and re-localized into the named signed covariance C(E) = Σ_{e∈[E,2E]} M(e)Δ_e as the single object any rung-2 continuation must compute with signs; I do not claim to control it.
obstacle_positions.fiber_growth: Avoided entirely, not solved. The mechanism lives in t-space (interval tilings and zero-density/explicit-formula inputs); no pair (d,d′,a,a′) → shared-modulus transfer is ever performed, so the linear-fiber counterexample has nothing to act on. Caveat: if one later expands the tail-block variance via Λ-correlations (MS singular-series route), modulus sums reappear and this obstacle re-engages; my deliverable stops before that door.
obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: Partially defused, and this is the lens's main structural point: the e-sum internally sweeps t = x/e over all of (y, x], so the variance factor is controlled by an average over t at FIXED x — no exceptional-set-in-x issue arises because no x-average is taken. Residual pin risk is real and localized: the sample points x/e are arithmetically synchronized with x, so the discrete tiling variance could conceivably exceed the continuous variance at this specific x (endpoint-resonance). The overlapping-interval comparison argument should absorb this, but that is exactly what kill test (b) probes.
obstacle_positions.modulus_magnitude: Not touched and not needed: no wheel modulus appears anywhere; all arithmetic inputs are zero-free-region and zero-density statements in the t-aspect. The obstacle is orthogonal to this mechanism.
obstacle_positions.parity: Parity-neutral by construction: μ enters only through |M(e)| or M(e)², never through a sieve construction, so the parity wall is not hit — but the price is stated plainly: discarding μ's sign past |M| is precisely why the route is 𝔉-capped at 3/4 even on RH inputs. Any parity-sensitive gain would have to come through C(E), outside this deliverable.
obstacle_positions.circularity: Clean. Zones (i)–(iii) use only Vinogradov–Korobov (PNT error), Landau/Walfisz (Mertens), and Huxley zero density — all unconditional; pointwise R(t) ≪ t^{1/2+ε} is never invoked, including for d = 1 (the d = 1 term sits in zone (i) and is bounded by VK-PNT only). Conditional variants (Selberg variance under RH, MS moments under Hardy–Littlewood) are quarantined as consistency checks and labeled as such.
obstacle_positions.finite_range: Complied with: numerics are used exclusively to kill (both kill tests are falsification probes on variance scale and pin-resonance), never to promote; the deliverable is an unconditional theorem with classical inputs. The packet's flat 0.35–0.43 cancellation coefficient is read only as motivation that C(E) is the right normalized object, not as evidence for any claim.

kill_test: Cheapest kill (a): at x ≈ 10⁸–10⁹ (data apparently already exists to 10⁹), compute the block tiling variances V(E) = Σ_{E<e≤2E} Δ_e² for dyadic E from 1 to √x and test them against the Selberg/MS continuous scale prediction V(E) ≍ X_w·(log X_w or log(X_w/H)) in the middle zone, and against the Poisson scale X_w/log x in the tail zone (H ≲ x^{1/11}, down to H ≈ 1 where Δ_e is essentially Bernoulli). If tail-zone or middle-zone V(E) systematically exceeds the continuous-variance scale by a growing factor, the discrete-to-continuous comparison — the load-bearing step — is dead and the angle dies. Secondary kill (b), pin-resonance: compare V(E) at the pinned x against the median of V(E) computed at ~50 nearby x′ ∈ [x, x + x/log x]; a persistent outlier at the pinned x kills the fixed-x comparison argument. Both tests are a few hundred lines of scripting on existing prime tables; hours, not weeks.
rung0_plan: Prove unconditionally |Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)R(⌊x/d⌋)| ≪ x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}), which is o() of the honest termwise trivial bound x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε})·log x (the log x factor and a constant are the gain; on the packet's own definition — o of the trivial scale — this is a rung-0 entrant). Steps: (1) zone (i), e ≤ E₀ = exp((log x)^{1/2}): termwise VK-PNT, cost E₀ terms each ≪ (x/e)δ, total ≪ x·δ·(log E₀) which is absorbed; (2) zone (iii), E > x^{5/11}: total-variation times max|M|, purely elementary given Landau/Walfisz; (3) zone (ii): the Saffari–Vaughan comparison plus Huxley-density variance — the only step with real analytic content, and it is a known-technology adaptation (variable interval length on a harmonic mesh), not a new estimate. Every ingredient is classical and citable; the assembly is bounded effort (weeks, one person). A cheaper fallback rung-0′ if the zone-(ii) variance adaptation stalls: run zones (i) and (iii) style bounds everywhere (termwise below x^{5/11}, total-variation above), which already yields x·δ_M·(log x)^{θ} with θ < 1 — a smaller but still real improvement over the trivial log x.
plausible_partial: Named partial, plausibly provable at bounded effort: THEOREM (Harmonic-tiling block decomposition, unconditional): |Σ_{d≤K} μ(d)R(⌊x/d⌋)| ≪ x·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5−ε}), via the three-zone assembly above; together with the standalone LEMMA (tiling-variance comparison): for E ≤ x^{5/11−ε}, the discrete reciprocal-interval variance Σ_{E<e≤2E} Δ_e² is bounded by an absolute constant times the continuous Saffari–Vaughan variance of the corresponding window plus an explicit error. The Lemma is independently publishable-adjacent and is the piece a rung-2 attack on C(E) would reuse. Honest assessment demanded by the prompt: this lens CANNOT touch rung 2 — the 𝔉-consistency computation shows second-moment recombination caps at x^{3/4} even with RH-strength inputs on both factors; the strongest defensible adjacent continuation (marked as such, not committed) is an MS-style singular-series evaluation of the signed covariance C(E), which is conditional on Hardy–Littlewood-type uniformity and re-engages obstacles 2 and 3.
self_assessed_risk: Weakest assumption, stated plainly: that unconditional Saffari–Vaughan-type variance with an exponential-in-(log)^c saving actually survives down to H = X_w^{1/6+ε} — the literature results near the shortest admissible H may only give o(H²X_w) rather than the exp saving I priced in, and the variable-length harmonic mesh comparison, while I believe it is a standard sub-blocking argument, is UNVERIFIED by me here. If the zone-(ii) saving degrades, the split point moves and the theorem weakens to the rung-0′ fallback but does not vanish. Overall risk: LOW-to-MODERATE for the rung-0 theorem (classical ingredients, one adaptation step); HIGH that the lens contributes nothing beyond rung 0 — near-certain failure at rung 2 through this mechanism, established by its own 𝔉-consistency check rather than by speculation. All capability claims above are unverified speculation per protocol.
